claims.claim: Title VII retaliation for internal harassment complaint
key_facts: Dana complained in writing on 2026-09-12 about her manager's repeated appearance and home/travel comments; an internal sexual-harassment complaint is protected opposition if the complaint concerns conduct made unlawful by Title VII.

The accused manager opened her first PIP on 2026-09-16, 4 days after the complaint (September 16 minus September 12 = 4 days), and HR proposed termination on 2026-10-06, 24 days after the complaint (October 6 minus September 12 = 24 days).
No prior discipline or PIP is recorded, and three same-role employees with lower 2026 YTD quota attainment had no PIP. The complaint has not been investigated.
The current record supports a strong circumstantial inference; it does not establish that the complaint actually caused the decision.

claims.claim: FMLA interference through termination to prevent requested leave
key_facts: Dana requested intermittent leave on 2026-09-30 to care for her mother after surgery and submitted medical certification on 2026-10-03; HR has not responded.
The proposed termination is 6 days after the request (October 6 minus September 30 = 6 days).

On 2026-10-02, Tom wrote: 'Let's get this done before she's out on leave. Once she's on FMLA it's a nightmare to move on her.' In Lena's follow-up, she reports that Tom still wants termination before leave. These statements directly link the proposed action to anticipated leave.
The legal claim depends on facts not supplied about employer coverage, Dana's eligibility, and the qualifying leave request; the risk assessment assumes the FMLA applies.

claims.claim: State of Columbia retaliation or termination for exercise of statutory rights
key_facts: Columbia's at-will rule has exceptions for retaliation and exercise of statutory rights and mirrors the federal protections in the supplied library.

The 4-day complaint-to-PIP interval, 6-day leave-request-to-proposed-termination interval, and manager's leave-related email support this risk, subject to the same factual prerequisites as the underlying rights.

claims.claim: Sex-based harassment and failure to investigate
key_facts: Dana reported repeated appearance comments and a question about whether she was too distracted at home to travel, but the precise words, frequency, witnesses, and context have not been investigated.
HR acknowledged the 2026-09-12 complaint but had opened no investigation by the proposed 2026-10-06 termination.

The supplied authority establishes a prompt, impartial investigation duty and that inaction undermines a potential employer defense; it does not establish from this record alone that the underlying conduct meets all elements of a harassment claim.

claims.claim: Age discrimination under the ADEA or comparable state law
key_facts: Dana is 42 and the three worse-performing employees without PIPs are 29, 31, and 35, which warrants review.
The record contains no age-related remark, and the other 40-plus comparator is 47, at 103% attainment, with no PIP; the data are too thin to establish an age-based reason.
The supplied ADEA library item addresses release validity, not the substantive elements of an age-discrimination claim; this merits investigation but no stronger legal conclusion from that authority.

separation_agreement_defects: For a 42-year-old employee, the seven-day consideration period is shorter than the OWBPA minimum of 21 days for an individual exit; if this is a covered group termination program, the minimum is 45 days. Group-program status has not been supplied.
The three-day revocation period is shorter than the required seven days after signing; an ADEA waiver cannot become effective until that period expires.
The draft does not advise Dana in writing to consult an attorney.
The blanket release is not expressly limited to claims arising through signing; an ADEA waiver cannot cover future claims.
The draft offers four weeks of base pay but does not establish whether that is additional consideration beyond amounts already owed.

These defects make the ADEA release unenforceable on the supplied authority; the employee may keep severance and sue on ADEA claims. Validity of other releases is not determined by the supplied library.
comparator_analysis: All four comparators are Account Managers. Dana: 88% 2026 YTD, PIP yes. Brennan: 79%, no PIP (88 - 79 = 9 percentage points lower); Osei: 84%, no PIP (88 - 84 = 4 points lower); Park: 86%, no PIP (88 - 86 = 2 points lower). All three are men under 40 with no recorded complaint. Lind, a 47-year-old woman, reached 103% and has no PIP, so her performance is less comparable. The same-role data materially weaken a quota-only explanation, but do not establish comparable territories, quotas, CRM hygiene, managers, tenure, or 2026 quarterly performance. Dana's 88% YTD figure and the PIP's 100% quarterly target are different measures and cannot be equated. The PIP opened September 16 for 60 days; only 20 days had elapsed by October 6 (October 6 minus September 16 = 20), leaving 40 days in the stated plan. No completed PIP assessment is in the record.
recommended_course: Do not terminate Dana on the proposed 2026-10-06 record or present the current release.

Immediately preserve relevant documents and electronic records; issue a hold to HR, Tom, decision-makers, and custodians of complaint, performance, comparator, and leave records, including email, texts, CRM data, and versions of the PIP.

Assign an impartial investigator outside Tom's chain of command to interview Dana, Tom, and witnesses; gather the comments and context; document findings and proportionate corrective action; protect Dana from retaliation.

Promptly process the FMLA request: verify coverage, eligibility, and certification; communicate the determination and any needed information; do not use the request or anticipated leave as a negative factor.

Remove Tom from decisions about Dana's discipline while an independent reviewer tests the PIP and quota/CRM rationale against objective records and genuinely comparable employees. Do not retroactively manufacture reasons or alter original records.

Reassess any employment action only after the complaint, leave request, and performance review are handled and a lawful, well-documented reason independent of protected activity is established; have counsel review the decision and a corrected agreement.
